- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% buffer to downward revisions.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent high); cap forecast at 1.2x recent high for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 14-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth 3-day moving average before final forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model misaligns with trend; align forecast to sentiment-weighted average of last 7 days.
